lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: everyday examples of conditional probability and independence
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: everyday examples of conditional probability and independence

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: P(A and B) = 3/20, P(B) = 5/20. Find P(A|B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 8/20, P(B) = 6/20, and P(A and B) = 4/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.

items.prompt: A box holds 10 items, of which 6 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 10/20 and P(B) = 11/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 22/100, P(B) = 13/100, and P(A and B) = 2/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 9 items, of which 4 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
